newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Labour's Shaw picks Act NZ above five percent.
newsitem.headline: Labour's Shaw picks Act NZ above five percent.

text.p: Oposition Labour Party Wellington Central candidate Alick Shaw predicted on Wednesday free-market Act New Zealand would break the five percent threshold and get seats in parliament.
Act has said it will support the incumbent National Party. It is averaging 4.8 percent in opinion polls ahead of the general election on October 12.

Act leader Richard Prebble is contesting Wellington Central in a close race with Shaw and the National candidate Mark Thomas. Some rebel National strategists have urged supporters to vote for Prebble to ensure a coalition partner for National. If
Act fails to make the five percent threshold it would need to win one of the 65 constituency seats to be sure of seats in parliament.
Speaking to a lunchtime forum at Victoria University Shaw said Act would not into parliament "through the backdoor of Wellington Central, but winning their five percent".
"If the National Party is returned it would not be business as usual," Shaw said. "Act would bring backbone to the right-wingers in the National government."
He said he was the only candidate that would keep both National and Act out.
Shaw said there would be uncertainty whether a centre-right or a centre-left government was elected in the general election on October 12.
He said a Labour-led government involving economic nationalist New Zealand First and the left-wing Alliance would be kept honest by the voters who put it there.

"There is nothing wrong at all with a government that does not have a complete programme. The fact that there are disagreements between those parties or even if Labour were there as a minority government, the fact that we do not have a complete programme agreed by all those on the centre-left is not
"What it means is that for once parliament might actually make some decisions... it might have to look at conflicting policies and decide which is best," Shaw said.
